question: In Nigeria's healthcare system, what level of care does a teaching hospital provide?
explanation: You've got this! Teaching hospitals and federal medical centres are at the very top of the referral chain, handling complex specialist care as tertiary facilities. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h1)

question: What is the main focus of Primary Health Centres (PHCs) in the community?

options.A: Preventive care and basic curative services

explanation: Spot on! PHCs are our grassroots centers focused on community health, immunizations, and treating everyday illnesses right where people live. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h1)

question: Where is the nurses' station usually placed in a standard hospital ward?

options.A: Positioned for clear visibility of patient beds
options.B: At the extreme corner of the isolation wing
options.D: Hidden away near the main hospital entrance

explanation: Great choice! Putting the nurses' station right in the middle lets staff keep a close eye on patients and jump into action quickly if an emergency pops up. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is a big perk of modern single-room wards compared to open-plan wards?

options.A: Requires fewer nurses to monitor patients
options.B: Eliminates the need for a dirty utility room
options.C: Lower cross-infection risks and better privacy
options.D: Cheaper overall construction and maintenance costs

explanation: Exactly! Private rooms keep patients separated, which stops germs from spreading easily while giving patients more peace and dignity. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h2)

question: Who carries the main administrative and clinical responsibility for running a hospital ward?
explanation: Well done! The Nursing Officer in Charge (NOIC) manages daily staffing, paperwork, and keeps care standards high on the unit. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h3)

question: A nurse needs to hand over a patient whose condition is getting worse to the incoming shift. Which communication tool is best to use?
explanation: You nailed it! SBAR keeps your handover clear and organized so no critical patient details get lost during shift change. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h3)

question: What activity usually happens right at the start of a new nursing shift on the ward?
explanation: Spot on! Incoming and outgoing nurses meet first for a handover briefing so everyone knows what's going on with every patient. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why do hospital wards stick to predictable daily routines?

options.A: They ensure treatments and observations happen on schedule
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for night shifts
options.C: They allow nurses to finish work hours ahead of time
options.D: They prevent doctors from visiting the ward unexpectedly

explanation: Correct! Good routines mean medications and vital signs aren't missed, helping both staff and patients stay on track. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is considered the single most effective way to stop hospital-acquired infections?
explanation: You got it! Washing or sanitizing your hands at the right moments is the number one shield against spreading germs. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h5)

question: Where should used surgical blades and injection needles be thrown away?

options.A: Open plastic basin on the treatment trolley

explanation: Safety first! Sharps always go into hard, puncture-proof boxes to keep everyone safe from accidental needle pricks. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h5)

question: What should a nurse do right away if they find a broken suction machine in the ward?

options.A: Tag it out of service and report it
options.B: Hide it inside the nurse's locker
options.C: Throw it into the domestic waste bin
options.D: Use it anyway on stable patients

explanation: Brilliant! Always label faulty gear clearly and report it so nobody tries to use a broken machine in an emergency. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why is keeping a regular inventory of ward supplies so important?

options.A: It allows nurses to sell extra medications for profit
options.B: It removes the need for equipment maintenance checks
options.C: It ensures doctors spend less time writing prescriptions
options.D: It prevents sudden stockouts of vital clinical supplies

explanation: Spot on! Tracking your stock ensures you never run out of dressings, drugs, or gloves when a patient needs them. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h6)

question: Which of these is a key step when admitting a brand new inpatient to the ward?

options.A: Verifying identity and recording baseline vitals
options.C: Collecting payment for next month's bills
options.D: Assigning them a permanent hospital job

explanation: You've got it! Checking ID stops mix-ups, and baseline vitals give you a starting point to track how well treatment is working. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h7)

question: What is the main goal of giving clear health education before a patient is discharged?

options.A: To delay the patient from leaving the hospital bed
options.B: To fulfill a bureaucratic administrative requirement
options.C: To promote recovery at home and prevent readmission
options.D: To test the patient's reading and writing skills

explanation: Right on! Good discharge teaching gives patients and families the confidence to care for themselves safely at home. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h7)
